description: Fills the user's TabTree KNOWLEDGE BASE — the "Company knowledge" map of a space — with its objects: projects, products, topics, clients, people, the company and its brands, partners. Each entry gets a short DEFINITION (what TabTree's card prompts read as context), its other names and a few facts. Use it when the user asks to fill or update their knowledge base, for example from their second brain. An entry that already exists (same name or alias, any section) is UPDATED, never duplicated. Nothing is written until the user accepts it in TabTree: one banner per call, one click applies it all. 30 entries per call at most — send several calls for more. Never a password, key or token.

entries.description: The objects to add or update, 30 at most.

aliases.description: Other names it goes by — old names, abbreviations, spellings (e.g. ["Nanomizer"]). 10 at most.

definition.description: What it is, in 2 to 5 sentences a newcomer understands: what it does, for whom, its status. This is the context every card prompt will carry. 1500 characters max.

facts.description: Short facts worth knowing, one per line — a price, a date, an owner, a link. "Name: value" lines become attributes. 20 at most, 300 characters each.

name.description: Its name, as people write it on cards — e.g. "Ai4Sales", "Hidden Tokens". 120 characters max.

section.description: Optional: an EXACT section name instead of `type` (read_map shows them). It must be an entry section — its name says projects, products, topics, clients, people, company, brands, partners or communities.

type.description: Which section it goes in: project, product, topic, client, person, company (the company and its brands) or partner (partners, communities, associations). Default: topic.

space.description: The space whose knowledge base to fill, by name (list_maps shows them). Omit for Personal. Knowledge never crosses spaces: if two could apply, ASK the user.

name: fill_knowledge
